name: Principles of Marketing
description: A systematic study of marketing principles — strategic marketing planning, consumer insights, brand management, integrated marketing communications, pricing strategy, and global marketing.

modules.title: Marketing Strategy & Planning
modules.objectives: Define marketing strategy; articulate a company mission; conduct a SWOT analysis; establish SMART marketing objectives and KPIs; map the strategic planning process. Students will evaluate realistic scenarios, apply concepts to decisions, and justify recommendations with evidence in the module assignment.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — strategic planning and the marketing plan
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: Create a one-page marketing plan for “StudySip,” a reusable bottle with a removable study-timer cap, priced at $24. Use this supplied context: a small team, a $12,000 launch budget, direct-to-consumer website, strong prototype reviews, no retail distribution, growing campus sustainability clubs, two established bottle brands, and copycat risk. Write a mission, classify each supplied fact in a SWOT, set three SMART objectives for the first 90 days, and assign two calculable KPIs to each objective. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: the supplied scenario, a correctly classified SWOT, three time-bound measurable objectives, six KPI formulas or definitions, and a short strategy rationale. Evaluation: 100% total — Marketing Strategy and Planning concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Consumer Insights & Research
modules.titleZh: 消费者洞察与市场调研
modules.objectives: Distinguish qualitative and quantitative research methods; design a basic consumer survey; analyze supplied survey and interview evidence; identify sampling limitations; interpret market research data to generate actionable insights.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — research methods and research-plan steps
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: Use this fictional StudySip research packet: survey n=120 (72% want leak resistance, 55% want timer reminders, 40% would pay $20–$29, 18% would pay $30+); interview excerpts: “I forget to drink while studying,” “another app notification would annoy me,” “I need it to fit a backpack,” “I would pay more if parts were replaceable.” Identify two quantitative and two qualitative findings, note one sampling limitation, write three neutral survey questions, and recommend one product and one messaging decision. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: a table separating quantitative from qualitative evidence, three neutral non-double-barreled questions, the sampling limitation, and two decisions explicitly tied to quoted or numeric evidence. Evaluation: 100% total — Consumer Research concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning (STP)
modules.titleZh: 市场细分、目标选择与定位（STP）
modules.objectives: Apply demographic, psychographic, behavioral, and geographic segmentation; evaluate targeting strategies; construct detailed buyer personas; draw and interpret perceptual maps; recommend repositioning strategies.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — segmentation, target-market selection, and positioning
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: StudySip is choosing among three segments: A campus commuters (8,000 people; high need for leak resistance; medium willingness to pay; high campus reach; medium competition), B fitness-club members (3,000; medium product fit; high willingness to pay; medium reach; high competition), C online graduate students (12,000; high need for reminder function; medium willingness to pay; low local reach; low competition). Use a 1–5 scoring scale, state how you convert each supplied label to a score, and label any remaining assumption rather than inventing data. Select one primary target using size, fit, reach, and competition. Build a persona. Then plot these supplied brands on a 1–5 map with axes “study support” and “price”: BasicBottle (1,2), EcoFlask (2,4), SmartHydrate (4,5), StudySip proposed (5,3). Write and justify a positioning statement. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: a scored target-selection table, persona tied to the selected segment, labeled perceptual map using all coordinates, positioning statement, and evidence-based justification. Evaluation: 100% total — Segmentation, Targeting, and Positioning concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Brand Management
modules.objectives: Define brand equity and its components; analyze brand architecture models; evaluate the risks and benefits of brand extensions; develop strategies for managing a brand across its lifecycle.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — brand development, extensions, loyalty, and metrics
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: Analyze a fictional parent brand, “Northstar Learning,” with three offers: Northstar Academy, Northstar Tutoring, and the proposed standalone “Spark Notes Lab.” Use this supplied guide: a branded house uses one master brand across offers; an endorsed brand gives a distinct offer its own identity while visibly linking it to the parent; a house of brands operates distinct consumer brands with little visible parent identity. Compare all three architectures. Recommend one architecture, assess two brand-extension benefits and two dilution/confusion risks, and give one metric for awareness, association, perceived quality, and loyalty at launch and six months. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: a three-model comparison, architecture recommendation, four risks/benefits, four defined brand-equity metrics, and a six-month measurement plan. Evaluation: 100% total — Brand Management concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Product Strategy
modules.objectives: Outline the new product development process; classify products within a portfolio using the BCG matrix; apply innovation frameworks; manage products through life cycle stages; evaluate product-line decisions.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — product life cycle and stage-specific strategy
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §10.2 — learn the stages of new-product development, including test marketing immediately before commercialization; pair it with the lifecycle reading.
modules.assignment: Use this supplied portfolio data: Core Bottle (relative market share 1.8, market growth 4%), Timer Cap (0.7, 18%), Filter Lid (0.4, 3%), Campus Bundle (1.3, 16%). For this exercise, define high relative market share as at least 1.0 and high market growth as at least 10%; values exactly on a cutoff count as high. Plot a BCG matrix and classify each item. For the Timer Cap, identify its product-life-cycle stage from this evidence: sales grew 45% this year, three competitors entered, awareness is rising, and margins remain positive. Recommend one resource-allocation decision and one stage-appropriate marketing action. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: a labeled BCG matrix with the supplied numerical cutoffs stated, four classifications, lifecycle diagnosis using the evidence, and two justified decisions. Evaluation: 100% total — Product Strategy concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Pricing Strategy (Advanced)
modules.objectives: Contrast cost-based, competition-based, and value-based pricing; explain psychological pricing tactics cautiously; calculate contribution margin and midpoint price elasticity of demand; recommend a price for a stated objective using supplied evidence.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §12.3 — pricing policy and elasticity. Correction for this course: inelastic demand means 0 < |PED| < 1; perfectly inelastic demand means PED = 0. Use the midpoint formula supplied in the assignment.
modules.videoNote: OpenStax visual lesson §12.5 — psychological pricing and pricing tactics for existing products; apply claims cautiously rather than assuming every buyer responds the same way.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: StudySip has unit variable cost $9, allocated fixed cost $6, current price $24, and 2,000 expected units. A survey estimates quantity demanded at 2,600 units at $21 and 1,700 at $27. Calculate contribution margin per unit and total contribution at $21, $24, and $27 using the supplied quantities (assume 2,000 units at $24). Use midpoint elasticity: [(Q2−Q1)/((Q1+Q2)/2)] ÷ [(P2−P1)/((P1+P2)/2)]. Calculate midpoint price elasticity between $21 and $27 and report its absolute value for classification while preserving the signed result. Recommend a price if the objective is total contribution, and identify one non-price concern. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: all formulas, substituted values, signed and absolute elasticity, a three-price contribution table, stated objective, and recommendation supported by the calculations. Evaluation: 100% total — Pricing Strategy concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Distribution & Channel Strategy
modules.objectives: Design a distribution channel; compare direct vs. indirect channels; evaluate omnichannel and multichannel strategies; explain logistics and supply chain roles in delivering customer value.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §17.3 — channel-choice factors and intensive, selective, and exclusive distribution
modules.videoNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §17.2 — direct and indirect channels and the difference between multichannel and integrated omnichannel distribution.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing §17.4 — channel management, conflict, cooperation, and disintermediation; apply the concepts to the supplied module scenario.
modules.assignment: Compare three StudySip channel plans using this supplied data: direct website—$8 contribution/unit, 2-day shipping to 70% of buyers, full customer data; campus bookstore—$4 contribution/unit, same-day access at 12 campuses, no individual customer data; marketplace—$5 contribution/unit, broad reach, 3–5 day shipping, partial data. Recommend a single, multichannel, or omnichannel design for the first semester. Map product, information, payment, and return flows and propose one inventory and one returns rule. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: a channel comparison table, accurate multichannel/omnichannel distinction, four labeled flows, two operating rules, and a decision tied to reach, margin, speed, and data. Evaluation: 100% total — Distribution and Channels concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

modules.title: Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC)
modules.objectives: Define IMC and explain why consistent messaging matters; coordinate advertising, PR, digital, and events into a unified campaign; create a basic IMC brief; measure communication effectiveness; adapt a core campaign for a supplied international-market scenario without losing message consistency.
modules.readingNote: OpenStax Principles of Marketing — promotion mix and communication process
modules.videoNote: Module-specific visual lesson or worked example; use it to check terminology and decision logic against the OpenStax reading.
modules.practiceNote: OpenStax worked lesson — apply the section framework to the supplied module scenario before completing the assignment.
modules.assignment: Plan a six-week $10,000 IMC launch for StudySip using these supplied channels: campus newsletter CPM $18, search ads CPC $1.80, creator package $2,500 with estimated 70,000 views, and club sampling $3 per unit. Use these fictional planning assumptions and treat each purchase as one new customer: newsletter—calculate impressions from CPM, use CTR 1.5%, then 3% click-to-purchase conversion; search—calculate clicks from CPC, then 4% click-to-purchase conversion (impressions and CTR are not applicable); creator—70,000 views count as impressions, link CTR is 0.8%, then 3% click-to-purchase conversion; club sampling—calculate samples from $3 per unit, then 12% sample-to-purchase conversion (impressions, clicks, and CTR are not applicable). Calculate channel CAC as allocated spend divided by that channel’s forecast new customers, and total campaign CAC as $10,000 divided by total forecast new customers. Set one awareness and one conversion objective, allocate the full budget, calculate each channel’s applicable impressions, clicks, samples, purchases, new customers, CTR, conversion rate, and CAC; mark the explicitly unavailable metrics “not applicable” using CPM = cost per 1,000 impressions and CPC = cost per click, write a consistent message adapted to each channel, Choose one supplied international-market scenario for a localized extension: Market A uses Spanish as the primary campaign language, requires metric units and local-language packaging, and relies mainly on mobile search; Market B uses Japanese as the primary campaign language, requires local-language packaging, and relies mainly on campus retail and messaging apps. Adapt the core promise, one channel execution, and one packaging disclosure for the selected market, and identify one assumption that would require local validation. and define and calculate with these supplied formulas: CTR = clicks/impressions, conversion rate = purchases/clicks, CAC = spend/new customers, plus one brand-lift measure with numeric targets. Submit: one PDF or document with clearly labeled sections and source links where used. Include: two SMART objectives, a budget totaling exactly $10,000, visible calculations using the supplied fictional forecast assumptions, channel-adapted messages with one core promise, a clearly labeled Market A or B localization, metric formulas, targets, and an optimization rule. Evaluation: 100% total — Integrated Marketing Communications concept accuracy and correct reasoning (40%); complete evidence, data, calculations, or examples (30%); justified decisions tied to the supplied scenario (20%); clear organization and source attribution (10%).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a SWOT analysis?
options: A financial statement summarizing company revenues
A framework analyzing Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats
A pricing model based on competitor benchmarks
A customer satisfaction measurement tool
questions.answer: A framework analyzing Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats
questions.explanation: SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats — a foundational strategic planning tool.

questions.question: A SMART marketing objective must be:
options: Simple, Measurable, Actionable, Relevant, Timely
Strategic, Marketing-focused, Attainable, Reviewed, Tested
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
Scalable, Manageable, Affordable, Realistic, Tactical
questions.answer: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
questions.explanation: SMART objectives are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound — ensuring clarity and accountability.

questions.question: Which research method collects non-numerical data through open-ended discussions?
options: Quantitative survey
Regression analysis
A/B testing
Qualitative research
questions.answer: Qualitative research
questions.explanation: Qualitative research (e.g., focus groups, in-depth interviews) gathers descriptive, non-numerical data to explore motivations and opinions.

questions.question: Choose the best answer: A perceptual map is used to:
options: Visualize how consumers perceive brands relative to each other on key attributes
Consumers perceive prices ending in .99 as significantly lower
Shifting how the target market perceives the brand relative to competitors
Consumers' age and gender
questions.answer: Visualize how consumers perceive brands relative to each other on key attributes
questions.explanation: The best answer is Visualize how consumers perceive brands relative to each other on key attributes.

questions.question: Psychographic segmentation divides markets based on:
options: Age, gender, and income
Lifestyle, values, and personality
Geographic location
Purchase frequency and brand loyalty
questions.answer: Lifestyle, values, and personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic segmentation focuses on psychological characteristics — lifestyle, interests, values, and attitudes.

questions.question: In Principles of Marketing midterm concepts, Brand equity refers to:
options: The total dollar value of a company's inventory
The number of SKUs in a product line
The additional value a brand name adds to a product beyond its functional attributes
The cost to register a trademark
questions.answer: The additional value a brand name adds to a product beyond its functional attributes
questions.explanation: Brand equity is the premium consumers are willing to pay or the loyalty they show due to the brand name itself.

questions.question: In the BCG matrix, which category has high relative market share in a low-growth market?
options: Star
Cash cow
Question mark
Dog
questions.answer: Cash cow
questions.explanation: A cash cow combines high relative market share with low market growth and may generate resources for other portfolio priorities.

questions.question: Choose the best answer: Value-based pricing sets price based on:
options: Total production cost plus a fixed markup
Charging all customers the same price regardless of location
The additional value a brand name adds to a product beyond its functional attributes
Customers' perceived value of the product or service
questions.answer: Customers' perceived value of the product or service
questions.explanation: The best answer is Customers' perceived value of the product or service. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Principles of Marketing midterm concepts.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes cost-based from value-based pricing?
options: Cost-based pricing starts from costs; value-based pricing starts from customers’ perceived value
Cost-based pricing ignores costs; value-based pricing uses only competitor prices
Both methods always produce the same price
Value-based pricing is illegal for premium brands
questions.answer: Cost-based pricing starts from costs; value-based pricing starts from customers’ perceived value
questions.explanation: Cost-based pricing adds a markup to cost, while value-based pricing estimates what benefits are worth to the target customer and checks whether the economics are viable.

questions.question: An omnichannel distribution strategy focuses on:
options: Selling only through a single retail chain
Providing a seamless customer experience across all physical and digital channels
Exporting products to multiple countries simultaneously
Reducing distribution costs by cutting intermediaries
questions.answer: Providing a seamless customer experience across all physical and digital channels
questions.explanation: Omnichannel integrates all channels so customers move fluidly between them (online, in-store, mobile) with a consistent experience.

questions.question: Which of the following is an internal factor in a SWOT analysis?
options: A new government regulation affecting the industry
An emerging competitor entering the market
The company's proprietary technology platform
A shift in consumer preferences toward sustainability
questions.answer: The company's proprietary technology platform
questions.explanation: Internal factors (Strengths and Weaknesses) are within the company's control — such as resources, capabilities, and processes.

questions.question: A company needs numerical estimates of purchase intent from 1,000 target customers. Which method best fits that purpose?
options: A five-person unstructured focus group
One executive interview
An analysis of two social-media comments
A structured survey using a probability sample
questions.answer: A structured survey using a probability sample
questions.explanation: A structured probability-sample survey can produce numerical estimates with a defensible sampling basis.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes segmentation from targeting?
options: Segmentation groups customers by shared characteristics; targeting selects which segment or segments the firm will serve
Segmentation chooses a price; targeting calculates cost
Segmentation designs advertisements; targeting measures inventory
They are two names for the same decision
questions.answer: Segmentation groups customers by shared characteristics; targeting selects which segment or segments the firm will serve
questions.explanation: For a fitness brand, runners and yoga practitioners could be segments; choosing one of them as the primary audience is targeting.

questions.question: Why can a price of $9.99 sometimes be perceived as lower than $10.00?
options: Consumers may anchor on the leftmost digit, making the price feel lower
It reduces company tax liability
It guarantees higher product quality
It is required by retail regulation
questions.answer: Consumers may anchor on the leftmost digit, making the price feel lower
questions.explanation: Left-digit effects can influence price perception in some contexts, but they do not guarantee a large response from every consumer.

questions.question: A premium coffee brand has $15 per pound in total unit cost and evidence that its target customers value traceable single-origin beans at about $30. Which pricing rationale best uses both cost and customer value?
options: Charge $15 because price must equal cost
Charge $30 only because a competitor does
Use $15 as an economic floor, then evaluate a $30 value-based price against willingness-to-pay evidence and brand positioning
Ignore cost because premium brands cannot lose money
questions.answer: Use $15 as an economic floor, then evaluate a $30 value-based price against willingness-to-pay evidence and brand positioning
questions.explanation: Cost evidence tests viability, while value evidence supports what the target customer may be willing to pay. A justified premium price considers both rather than applying an automatic markup.

questions.question: After a company has established its mission, which step should come before setting detailed marketing objectives?
options: Set marketing objectives
Conducting a situation analysis
It eliminates the need for a marketing budget
The total budget allocated to a marketing campaign
questions.answer: Conducting a situation analysis
questions.explanation: With mission already established, a situation analysis examines internal and external conditions before the firm sets detailed marketing objectives and tactics.

questions.question: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is best described as:
options: A qualitative statement of company values
The total budget allocated to a marketing campaign
A measurable metric used to evaluate progress toward a specific objective
A list of competitor weaknesses
questions.answer: A measurable metric used to evaluate progress toward a specific objective
questions.explanation: KPIs are quantifiable measures that track performance against stated goals (e.g., website conversion rate, cost per acquisition).

questions.question: A focus group is MOST useful for:
options: Measuring the statistical significance of consumer preferences
Calculating market size for a new product category
Projecting annual sales revenue
Exploring consumer attitudes and motivations in depth
questions.answer: Exploring consumer attitudes and motivations in depth
questions.explanation: Focus groups are qualitative tools — they surface rich verbal and emotional data, not statistically representative conclusions.

questions.question: Repositioning a brand means:
options: Shifting how the target market perceives the brand relative to competitors
Changing the physical location of company headquarters
Replacing the entire product line with new SKUs
Reducing the price to capture a lower-income segment
questions.answer: Shifting how the target market perceives the brand relative to competitors
questions.explanation: Repositioning alters the brand's perceived place in consumers' minds — often to reach a new segment or respond to competitive pressure.

questions.question: Choose the best answer: Which Keller CBBE model layer represents the functional benefits a brand delivers?
options: Google, which uses the Google brand for all services
Brand Meaning (Performance & Imagery)
The additional value a brand name adds to a product beyond its functional attributes
The font and color palette used in brand identity
questions.answer: Brand Meaning (Performance & Imagery)
questions.explanation: The best answer is Brand Meaning (Performance & Imagery). Students need to recognize why Brand Meaning (Performance & Imagery) matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: A product in the BCG 'Dog' quadrant should typically be:
options: Invested in heavily to grow market share
Turned into a Star through aggressive promotion
Divested, discontinued, or managed for residual cash
Repositioned as a premium offering
questions.answer: Divested, discontinued, or managed for residual cash
questions.explanation: Dogs have low share in low-growth markets — they generate little return and often drain resources, making divestment the rational choice.

questions.question: Price elasticity of demand (PED) greater than 1 (|PED| > 1) indicates:
options: Demand is inelastic — price changes have little effect on quantity demanded
The product is a luxury good with exclusive demand
Supply increases faster than demand
Demand is elastic — consumers are highly sensitive to price changes
questions.answer: Demand is elastic — consumers are highly sensitive to price changes
questions.explanation: When |PED| > 1, a 1% price increase causes more than a 1% drop in quantity demanded — consumers are price-sensitive.

questions.question: An indirect distribution channel includes:
options: A producer using wholesalers and retailers to reach end consumers
A manufacturer selling directly to consumers via its own website
A company delivering products through its own fleet
A subscription box shipped factory-direct
questions.answer: A producer using wholesalers and retailers to reach end consumers
questions.explanation: Indirect channels involve one or more intermediaries (wholesalers, distributors, retailers) between producer and consumer.

questions.question: Choose the best answer: The primary goal of Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) is to:
options: Maximize spending across all media channels equally
Coordinate messages across channels so the brand communicates consistently
It eliminates the need for a marketing budget
The font and color palette used in brand identity
questions.answer: Coordinate messages across channels so the brand communicates consistently
questions.explanation: The best answer is Coordinate messages across channels so the brand communicates consistently.

questions.question: In advertising, 'reach' refers to:
options: The number of times an average person sees an ad
The geographic territory covered by a campaign
The total number of unique individuals exposed to an ad
The creative length of a video advertisement
questions.answer: The total number of unique individuals exposed to an ad
questions.explanation: Reach measures how many different people are exposed to a message at least once; frequency measures how often.

questions.question: A/B testing in digital marketing involves:
options: Testing a product in two countries before global launch
Running ads on two platforms simultaneously with the same creative
Comparing two fiscal quarters of marketing spend
Comparing two versions of a campaign element to determine which performs better
questions.answer: Comparing two versions of a campaign element to determine which performs better
questions.explanation: A/B testing isolates one variable (e.g., email subject line, ad image) and measures which version drives better results.

questions.question: Which expression gives contribution margin per unit?
options: Price − variable cost
Price − fixed cost
Revenue ÷ impressions
Fixed cost ÷ units
questions.answer: Price − variable cost
questions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit is selling price minus variable cost. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.

questions.question: A retailer sells through its website and campus stores but inventory and returns are managed separately. This is best described as:
options: Single-channel
Multichannel
Omnichannel
Direct-only
questions.answer: Multichannel
questions.explanation: The firm uses multiple channels, but the experience is not integrated enough to be omnichannel.

questions.question: Which metric measures clicks as a percentage of ad impressions?
options: Reach
Customer lifetime value
Click-through rate
Market share
questions.answer: Click-through rate
questions.explanation: CTR = clicks divided by impressions, usually expressed as a percentage. The denominator is impressions, not unique viewers, because one person may receive multiple impressions.

questions.question: A positioning statement should primarily explain:
options: Only the production cost
Every feature a product has
The legal structure of the company
The target customer, frame of reference, distinctive benefit, and reason to believe
questions.answer: The target customer, frame of reference, distinctive benefit, and reason to believe
questions.explanation: A useful positioning statement identifies whom the offer serves and why it is meaningfully different.

questions.question: In the new product development process, which stage immediately precedes commercialization?
options: Test marketing
Idea generation
Concept testing
Business analysis
questions.answer: Test marketing
questions.explanation: Test marketing introduces the product in a limited area to gauge real-world performance before full-scale commercialization.

questions.question: A product price is $40 and variable cost is $16. What is its contribution margin per unit?
questions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit = price − variable cost = $40 − $16 = $24. This calculation uses the course definition and separates per-unit contribution from total revenue, fixed cost, or selling price.

questions.question: When comparing two channel options, which set of evidence is most relevant?
options: Logo color only
The CEO’s favorite store
Reach, margin, delivery speed, control, and customer data
The number of product features
questions.answer: Reach, margin, delivery speed, control, and customer data
questions.explanation: Channel design requires economic and customer-experience evidence. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.

questions.question: Which plan correctly applies segmentation, targeting, and positioning for a premium yoga class?
options: Segment by lifestyle and experience; target working professionals seeking stress relief; position the class as a small-group premium restorative experience
Choose a slogan; lower every price; then copy competitors
Target everyone; avoid segments; use no distinct benefit
Position first without a target; then remove all customer research
questions.answer: Segment by lifestyle and experience; target working professionals seeking stress relief; position the class as a small-group premium restorative experience
questions.explanation: The plan first identifies meaningful groups, selects a specific audience, and then defines a distinctive benefit for that audience, matching the STP sequence.

questions.question: A campaign spends $6,000 and acquires 300 new customers. What is customer acquisition cost?
questions.explanation: CAC = campaign cost/new customers = $6,000/300 = $20. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is an example of an external opportunity in a SWOT analysis?
options: A competitor exiting the market
A skilled internal marketing team
High employee turnover
An outdated company website
quizQuestions.answer: A competitor exiting the market
quizQuestions.explanation: Opportunities are external factors the company can exploit — a competitor leaving the market opens up market share.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a KPI for a brand awareness campaign?
options: Number of employees hired
Unaided brand recall rate
Production cost per unit
Supplier lead time
quizQuestions.answer: Unaided brand recall rate
quizQuestions.explanation: Unaided brand recall measures how many consumers think of the brand without prompting — directly tied to awareness objectives.

quizQuestions.question: Which objective is SMART for StudySip’s first 90 days?
options: Increase awareness
Become the best bottle brand
Raise aided awareness among surveyed campus commuters from 10% to 25% by day 90
Post more often on social media
quizQuestions.answer: Raise aided awareness among surveyed campus commuters from 10% to 25% by day 90
quizQuestions.explanation: It is specific, measurable, relevant, and time-bound. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is a quantitative research method?
options: In-depth interviews
Ethnographic observation
Focus group discussion
Online survey with Likert-scale questions
quizQuestions.answer: Online survey with Likert-scale questions
quizQuestions.explanation: Quantitative research collects numerical data that can be statistically analyzed — surveys with rating scales are a primary example.

quizQuestions.question: A focus group typically consists of:
options: 6–10 participants discussing a topic guided by a moderator
100–200 randomly selected consumers completing a written survey
One researcher conducting deep one-on-one interviews
A team of executives brainstorming product ideas
quizQuestions.answer: 6–10 participants discussing a topic guided by a moderator
quizQuestions.explanation: Focus groups bring together a small number of representative consumers to explore attitudes, perceptions, and motivations in guided discussion.

quizQuestions.question: Secondary market research uses data that:
options: Is collected directly from consumers for the first time
Already exists and was gathered for another purpose
Can only be obtained through focus groups
Requires a minimum sample size of 1,000 respondents
quizQuestions.answer: Already exists and was gathered for another purpose
quizQuestions.explanation: Secondary research draws from existing sources (industry reports, government statistics, published studies) vs. primary research collected firsthand.

quizQuestions.question: A survey link is posted only to a brand’s most active fan group. What is the main research risk?
options: Random assignment
Selection bias from an unrepresentative convenience sample
Perfect external validity
Experimental control
quizQuestions.answer: Selection bias from an unrepresentative convenience sample
quizQuestions.explanation: Highly engaged fans may differ systematically from the target market, so their responses may not represent all potential customers. This affects how far the survey result can be generalized.

quizQuestions.question: Behavioral segmentation divides the market based on:
options: Consumers' physical location
Consumers' age and gender
Consumers' values and lifestyle preferences
Usage rate, loyalty, and purchase occasion
quizQuestions.answer: Usage rate, loyalty, and purchase occasion
quizQuestions.explanation: Behavioral segmentation groups consumers by how they interact with a product — heavy/light users, brand loyalists, occasion-based buyers.

quizQuestions.question: In Segmentation, Targeting & Positioning (STP), A buyer persona is:
options: A semi-fictional profile representing a typical target customer
A legal document representing a consumer complaint
A database of all current customers' contact information
A demographic breakdown of an entire country
quizQuestions.answer: A semi-fictional profile representing a typical target customer
quizQuestions.explanation: Personas synthesize research into a vivid character — name, goals, pain points, behaviors — to guide marketing decisions.

quizQuestions.question: Differentiated targeting means a company:
options: Targets the entire market with one offering
Targets multiple segments with distinct marketing mixes for each
Targets only one narrow niche segment
Personalizes messaging to every individual customer
quizQuestions.answer: Targets multiple segments with distinct marketing mixes for each
quizQuestions.explanation: Differentiated (multi-segment) targeting tailors the product, price, promotion, and distribution to each chosen segment.

quizQuestions.question: Brand architecture refers to:
options: The physical design of a company's office buildings
The font and color palette used in brand identity
The structure that organizes a company's portfolio of brands and products
The number of employees in the marketing department
quizQuestions.answer: The structure that organizes a company's portfolio of brands and products
quizQuestions.explanation: Brand architecture defines how a parent brand and sub-brands relate — e.g., branded house (Virgin), house of brands (Procter & Gamble).

quizQuestions.question: A brand extension is MOST risky when:
options: The new product category is closely related to the parent brand's core
The extension leverages existing brand equity with the same consumers
The parent brand has strong awareness and loyalty
The new category is far removed from the parent brand's identity and competency
quizQuestions.answer: The new category is far removed from the parent brand's identity and competency
quizQuestions.explanation: Distant extensions can dilute brand equity and confuse consumers — e.g., a luxury fashion brand launching fast food.

quizQuestions.question: Brand equity can be built through:
options: Consistent messaging, quality, and positive consumer experiences over time
Frequent price discounting to attract new customers
Changing the brand name and logo every year to stay fresh
Copying competitor brand strategies
quizQuestions.answer: Consistent messaging, quality, and positive consumer experiences over time
quizQuestions.explanation: Brand equity accumulates through repeated, reliable, and positive brand interactions that build awareness, associations, and loyalty.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the following is an example of a 'house of brands' architecture?
options: Apple, which brands all products under the Apple name
Procter & Gamble, which markets Tide, Pampers, and Gillette as separate brands
Google, which uses the Google brand for all services
Virgin, which names all ventures with the Virgin prefix
quizQuestions.answer: Procter & Gamble, which markets Tide, Pampers, and Gillette as separate brands
quizQuestions.explanation: A house of brands keeps parent company identity in the background; each brand is independent with its own positioning.

quizQuestions.question: In the BCG matrix, a 'Star' product is characterized by:
options: Low market share and high market growth
High market share and low market growth
High market share and high market growth
Low market share and low market growth
quizQuestions.answer: High market share and high market growth
quizQuestions.explanation: Stars lead in fast-growing markets — they require investment to sustain growth but have the potential to become Cash Cows.

quizQuestions.question: The product life cycle stage with the fastest sales growth and increasing competition is:
options: Introduction
Maturity
Decline
Growth
quizQuestions.answer: Growth
quizQuestions.explanation: In the growth stage, early adopters spread the word, sales accelerate, and competitors enter — requiring investment in differentiation.

quizQuestions.question: A product with low relative market share in a high-growth market is classified in the BCG matrix as a:
options: Question mark
Star
Cash cow
Dog
quizQuestions.answer: Question mark
quizQuestions.explanation: Question marks operate in high-growth markets but have low relative share. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.

quizQuestions.question: During the growth stage of the product life cycle, a common strategic priority is to:
options: Eliminate all promotion
Build preference and expand distribution as competitors enter
Harvest immediately regardless of demand
Stop improving the product
quizQuestions.answer: Build preference and expand distribution as competitors enter
quizQuestions.explanation: Growth brings rising sales and competition, making differentiation and availability important.

quizQuestions.question: Cost-plus pricing sets the selling price by:
options: Surveying what customers are willing to pay
Matching the leading competitor's price
Adding a fixed markup percentage to the cost of production
Using demand forecasts to maximize revenue
quizQuestions.answer: Adding a fixed markup percentage to the cost of production
quizQuestions.explanation: Cost-plus pricing: Price = Cost + (Cost × Markup%). Simple to apply but ignores market demand and perceived value.

quizQuestions.question: Price elasticity of demand (PED) = −2 means:
options: A 1% price increase leads to a 0.5% decrease in quantity demanded
Price has no effect on demand
Demand increases as price increases
A 1% price increase leads to a 2% decrease in quantity demanded
quizQuestions.answer: A 1% price increase leads to a 2% decrease in quantity demanded
quizQuestions.explanation: PED = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price. PED = −2 means demand is elastic — very sensitive to price.

quizQuestions.question: A product sells for $25 and has a variable cost of $10 per unit. What is its contribution margin per unit?
quizQuestions.explanation: Contribution margin per unit equals price minus variable cost: $25 − $10 = $15. It is the amount available to cover fixed costs and profit.

quizQuestions.question: Using the midpoint method, demand is called elastic when the absolute value of price elasticity is:
options: less than 0
greater than 1
less than 1
equal to 0
quizQuestions.answer: greater than 1
quizQuestions.explanation: Demand is elastic when the percentage quantity response exceeds the percentage price change, so |PED| > 1.

quizQuestions.question: A new company sets a deliberately low introductory price to gain market share quickly. Which strategy is this?
options: Price skimming
Penetration pricing
Bundle pricing
Prestige pricing
quizQuestions.answer: Penetration pricing
quizQuestions.explanation: Penetration pricing uses a low launch price to accelerate adoption and market-share growth; the firm must still assess whether the economics and later price path are sustainable.

quizQuestions.question: Which distribution intensity strategy uses ONLY ONE retailer per geographic area?
options: Intensive distribution
Selective distribution
Exclusive distribution
Direct distribution
quizQuestions.answer: Exclusive distribution
quizQuestions.explanation: Exclusive distribution gives a single retailer or dealer exclusive rights in a territory — common for luxury and specialty brands.

quizQuestions.question: Disintermediation in a distribution channel means:
options: Adding more intermediaries to increase market coverage
Switching from online to physical retail
Outsourcing logistics to a third-party provider
Removing intermediaries so producers sell directly to consumers
quizQuestions.answer: Removing intermediaries so producers sell directly to consumers
quizQuestions.explanation: Disintermediation can reduce intermediary fees and may increase producer margin, but only if the producer can replace fulfillment, acquisition, inventory, and service functions at an acceptable total cost.

quizQuestions.question: Which statement best distinguishes omnichannel from multichannel distribution?
options: Omnichannel coordinates channels into a connected customer experience
Omnichannel uses only stores
Multichannel always shares inventory data
They mean exactly the same thing
quizQuestions.answer: Omnichannel coordinates channels into a connected customer experience
quizQuestions.explanation: Multichannel uses more than one channel; omnichannel integrates them across the customer journey.

quizQuestions.question: The 'promotional mix' in IMC typically includes which of the following elements?
options: Product, Price, Place, Promotion
Advertising, Public Relations, Personal Selling, Sales Promotion, Direct Marketing
Reach, Frequency, Impressions, Conversions
Mission, Vision, Values, Strategy
quizQuestions.answer: Advertising, Public Relations, Personal Selling, Sales Promotion, Direct Marketing
quizQuestions.explanation: The promotional mix (part of the 4Ps' Promotion) combines these tools to communicate the brand message to the target audience.

quizQuestions.question: Message consistency across all IMC channels is critical because:
options: It reduces the number of employees needed in marketing
Regulations require identical messages on all platforms
Inconsistent messages confuse consumers and erode brand trust
It eliminates the need for a marketing budget
quizQuestions.answer: Inconsistent messages confuse consumers and erode brand trust
quizQuestions.explanation: When different channels send conflicting signals, consumers lose confidence in the brand — IMC ensures a coherent, reinforcing narrative.

quizQuestions.question: Public Relations (PR) in an IMC campaign is most valuable for:
options: Directly selling products through a sales force
Running paid display ads on social media platforms
Setting the product's retail price
Building credibility and managing brand reputation through earned media
quizQuestions.answer: Building credibility and managing brand reputation through earned media
quizQuestions.explanation: PR earns media coverage through newsworthy stories — third-party editorial endorsement carries more credibility than paid advertising.

quizQuestions.question: A campaign receives 2,000 clicks and 80 purchases. What is the click-to-purchase conversion rate?
quizQuestions.explanation: Conversion rate = 80/2,000 × 100% = 4%. This choice uses the module definition and connects the decision to measurable evidence rather than an unsupported preference.
